title: "1 in 3" Beats 33%
objective: After this level you can switch between percentages, fractions and "1 in N" counts, and explain why counts of people are easier to picture.
summary: "1 in N" is 100 ÷ N percent, so 1 in 4 is 25% and a bigger N means a smaller share. Simple counts like "2 in 5" are easier to picture than percents, especially with the same bottom number.

cards.headline: In the 1980s, a burger flopped because 3 looks smaller than 4.
cards.body: A&W sold a third-pound burger for the same price as McDonald's Quarter Pounder. More meat, same money. According to A. Alfred Taubman, A&W's owner at the time, focus groups asked why they should pay the same for less. Many thought a third was smaller than a quarter.

cards.headline: Three ways to say one share
cards.body: 1 in 4, one quarter and 25% are the same share. To turn "1 in N" into a percent, divide 100 by N: 1 in 4 is 25%, 1 in 5 is 20%, 1 in 3 is about 33%. To go back, divide 100 by the percent. And notice the twist that sank the burger: in "1 in N", a bigger N means a smaller share. A third (1 in 3) beats a quarter (1 in 4).

cards.headline: Counts of people are easier to picture
cards.body: Some studies suggest patients grasp simple counts, like "2 in 5", better than "40 percent". Same share, different picture. A percent is an abstract slice of a hundred; a count gives you people to imagine. Two people in a room of five is something your mind can actually see.

cards.fact: Best of all: counts with the same bottom number.
cards.context: Is 1 in 12 more than 1 in 17? It takes a moment. Put both over 50, about 4 in 50 against 3 in 50, and the answer is instant. Risk experts advise exactly that. They also warn that a lone "1 in X" can make a risk seem bigger than it is.

cards.headline: "1 in N": translated
learned: Bigger N means a smaller share
Counts of people are easier to picture
Compare with the same bottom number

questions.explanation: Divide 100 by the percent: 100 ÷ 20 = 5, so 20% is 1 in 5.

questions.prompt: Match each "1 in N" with its percent.
questions.explanation: Divide 100 by N: 1 in 4 is 25%, 1 in 5 is 20%, and 1 in 3 is about 33%.

questions.prompt: One leaflet says a side effect affects 1 in 12 people; another says 1 in 17. What makes them easiest to compare?

options.label: Pick whichever leaflet shows the bigger number
options.rationale: In "1 in N" the bigger N is the smaller risk; that invites mistakes.

options.label: Ignore the counts and trust your gut
options.rationale: Putting both on one scale beats guessing.

options.label: Only look at the 1 in each
options.rationale: The 1 is the same; the bottom numbers carry the difference.

options.label: Put both over one number: about 4 in 50 and 3 in 50

questions.explanation: Just as Level 2's percents put groups on one scale, a shared bottom number (about 4 in 50 vs 3 in 50) makes the comparison instant.
